To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
parents of children on the Autistic spectrum experience a great deal of emotional labour in caring for their children, which is a labour of love.

parents of children with ASD experience emotional exhaustion and fatigue, as a result of their children’s needs, which are often unmet, and that the children’s needs are often not met due to a lack of understanding of the condition and the triad of impairments.
parents of children with autistic spectrum disorders (ASD) are often exhausted and emotionally drained.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of autism on the lives of those involved, including the parents and carers, the child and the wider family.
the emotional impact, including fatigue and stress, associated with the caring of children on the Autistic spectrum.
the emotional impact, and fatigue, stress and inter-related symptoms, of parenting children with autistic spectrum disorders (ASD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this research highlights the emotional work involved in parenting children with autism spectrum disroders, which has a significant and detrimental psychological impact upon the parents.

this research has illuminated how parenting those with autism can be an emotionally demanding and challenging role for parents, and that the impact of the emotional work associated with this role can be significant.

, in order to reduce the impact of the ‘burden’ of parenting children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), there is a need for greater awareness of the implications, and possible context, for the implementation of education and social work interventions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it has highlighted the emotional impact of parenting children on the autistic spectum, and has illuminated the need for greater awareness of the impact of this emotional labour of love, and the need for greater support, training, respite care, and a greater understanding of the needs of those on the autistic specturm.
the project has illuminated the emotional impact of parenting children with autistic spectrum disorders, which has implications for social work practice and education.
this project has highlighted the need for further research into the psychological impact of the emotional work of parenting children on the autistic specturm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emotional work associated with parenting children with autism spectrum disorder is a significant factor in the overall well-being of the family unit.
the emotional work associated with parenting those with autistic disorders can be draining, and can lead to fatigue, stress and a host of inter-related symptoms.

there is a need for further research into the emotional impact of the emotional work of parenting those on the autistic spectrum; and the need for more support for parents, and others involved in caring for those on the autistic spectrum.
